kind: the edits, proven by violation in both directions, merged and then proven on the deployed surface
headline: The preamble's rule 3 now holds on all eight request-scoped routes and all four module-level defaults, and a bare visit no longer lands on the demo pack. Measured on the deployed d12-main-uat: 7 of 7 probeable routes refuse a request that names no city with 400 city_key_required, and the bare visit renders the stated no-city panel with the demo pack's name nowhere in the document. The pre-fix leg is captured on the same URL because that window cannot be reopened.

uatApp.name: d12-main-uat
uatApp.previousDeployment: 939947a9-4445-4cd1-8381-a40274ddabf7 at 53ade8a9dbdb649acbe04c721a54fa518779d0b1 - the PRE-G-161 commit, retained in the record because it served the pre-fix probe leg
uatApp.howTheMergeBecameADeployment: It did not, and a lane that assumed otherwise would have read back the previous commit and called it proof. services[0].github carries repo+branch only - no deploy_on_push - so the merge produced no deployment and an explicit apps-update with update_all_source_versions true was required. The hash was then read back AND compared against git rev-parse origin/main, which is a different act from reading it.
uatApp.nonProduction: Non-production proof target only. Nothing was deployed to v1, to walrus-app, or to the GCP rollback copy.

server.oneRefusalStatedOnce: requiredCityKey(res, url, stake) replaces the eight copies of the same three-line guard. It trims BEFORE it tests, so ?cityKey=%20 names nothing and is refused rather than treated as absent-and-fine, and it returns the trimmed key so no call site re-reads the query string. `stake` is the sentence the route contributes and is REQUIRED rather than defaulted, so a call site added later has to say what its own 400 is protecting rather than inheriting a vague sentence from its neighbour.

routesNowRefusing.was: || DEFAULT_CITY_KEY - a SYMBOL, so a grep for the literal misses it entirely
|| "template-city" - one handler behind every domain endpoint of the seven lenses, so this default reached further than any other line on the list
|| "template-city" - the route that NAMES the city on the surface, so the default stamped the demo city's name, seal and palette on a caller who had named none
|| "template-city", 403-guarded so it could not serve another city - but a keyless caller still RAN the demo pack's calendar and WROTE its files

server.routePrecedenceKept: The municode POST still checks its caller first (401), then the request (400), then the pack (403). The refusal is about the REQUEST, so it does not come before the authorization of the CALLER: a request naming no city is malformed whatever identity presents it.
server.statusCode: 400, not 404. An ABSENT pack and an UNKNOWN pack are different findings and stay distinguishable; a named readable pack answers exactly as before.
server.cityPacksRoute: GET /api/city-packs now returns `caller: { kind, tenant }` alongside the list. This is what makes the client's second resolution leg possible at all: a Hauska product key or a staff sign-in names the city SERVER-side, and web/app.js is forbidden by src/city-identity.test.mjs from carrying any shipped pack's key as a literal. `tenant` is null for a caller who is the subject of nothing, which is a real state rather than an error, so a blank is never read as a city.

allFourGone.what: DEFAULT_CITY_KEY deleted; composeCityManager no longer defaults its parameter and THROWS on a missing or empty cityKey. The throw is a contract guard, not the refusal path - src/server.mjs refuses first - and it exists so a call site added later cannot silently default by forgetting an argument.
Its own DEFAULT_CITY_KEY deleted; resolveStaffMapQuery returns an EMPTY cityKey rather than the demo. This is the line that made a bare visit land on the demo.
The cityKey parameter default is gone; the function throws rather than running the demo pack's calendar.
The CLI default is gone; it prints usage to stderr and exits 2 rather than writing the demo pack's calendar for a run nobody aimed at it.

client.resolutionOrder: 1. an EXPLICIT ?cityKey, already resolved by resolveStaffMapQuery. 2. otherwise the CALLER'S OWN RESOLVED TENANT, read from GET /api/city-packs - the one route the client may call WITHOUT naming a city, because it is an enumeration and it resolves the caller. 3. otherwise NOTHING, and no loader is called at all.
client.neverSendsAnEmptyKey: A keyless route call is a 400 as of this lane, so the client never sends an empty cityKey to any route. The twelve loaders sit on one side of one branch (`if (staffMap.cityKey) { ... } else { showNoCityState(); }`), which is the difference between a surface that reads no city and a surface that fires twelve failing requests and renders 'not read' for each of them as though the city had answered.
client.chromeStaysOutsideTheBranch: The menu, theme toggle, compass and top menus are the PRODUCT's controls rather than any city's, so a no-city surface is still operable.
client.navThreading: The guard is now `if (staffMap.cityKey)` rather than `!== DEFAULT_CITY_KEY`. A pack named explicitly - including the demo pack - keeps its visitor on that pack, and a no-city visit keeps the static hrefs, which carry no city, which is right because the next page is a no-city page too.
client.thePanel: web/index.html ships #no-city-state hidden, so a browser with scripting off still sees the one lens the static markup turns on (G-89). It names no city and carries no pack hook: a name there would be exactly the invention this lane deletes. It is revealed by showNoCityState() in the same step that hides every .lens, so the two can never both be on screen, and it is hidden with the bare [hidden] attribute because web/shell.css carries one rule that outranks the lens show/hide enumeration and a second visibility mechanism for one question is a defect that comment says has already been paid for twice.

theInstrumentThatHadToChangeWithIt.what: The gate built its 24 targets WITHOUT a cityKey, on the strength of the client resolving a default for them. That URL now renders the no-city panel, so the gate would have measured one panel 24 times rather than 24 surfaces, and would have been RED on every title, because the pack's name is part of the title and nothing would have put it there.
theInstrumentThatHadToChangeWithIt.fix: Every target names its pack, so all 24 carry a cityKey explicitly (23 the default pack, 1 empty-city). `target()` defaults the pack rather than each call site naming it, so a target added later cannot forget it.
theInstrumentThatHadToChangeWithIt.secondFixInTheSameFile: expectedTitle looked the pack up in SCANNED_PACKS, which is [empty-city] - the default pack is NOT a scanned pack. That was harmless while only the pack targets carried a key and became load-bearing the moment every target did: the old lookup would have dropped the pack's name out of 23 of the 24 expected titles while looking like a deliberate answer. It now resolves against a map of every pack the file knows (the two scanned, plus the one it excludes by name), and a target naming a pack the file has no pack for THROWS by name rather than returning a title with no pack in it.
theInstrumentThatHadToChangeWithIt.proven: src/a11y-gate.test.mjs holds it as a property of the LIST rather than by reading the one place that builds it: a target with no pack is caught wherever it came from, and the assertion is shown able to fire by injecting one target into the list and getting its name back. It also asserts the pack is really IN the expected title, not just in the params, and that an unknown key throws.
theInstrumentThatHadToChangeWithIt.andTheWholeGateWasRunGreen: The unit-level property above is not the only evidence. The gate was run END TO END against the real product in this worktree before the push: `npm run test:a11y` exited 0 across all 24 now-named surfaces, 2026-09-18T15:18:39Z to 15:43:14Z (~24.6 min, against CI's 8m20s on the same commit - the same gate, a slower machine). Filed because this section's claim is that a surface NOT named in the dispatch had to change, and a green whole-gate run is what shows the change traded one red for another rather than just moving it. Its output file was scratch and was deleted in worktree cleanup, so the exit code and the window survive in the terminal record; the durable copy is the same gate PASSING in CI at the merged commit.

runner.result: 12 of 12 pass. Measured in this worktree at the lane commit.
runner.routeHarness: 8 routes x {absent, empty, whitespace, named, unknown, tenant-private} over REAL HTTP against a booted server, asserting the REFUSAL CLASS of each cell rather than a status code alone. For the refused cells it also asserts that no payload came back with the refusal, and specifically that a refused /api/city-identity carries no cityKey and no identity field - because the old behaviour was a complete, well-formed 200 that nothing else could distinguish from a real pack's answer.
runner.theControlThatKeepsItFromBeingAnOutage: The same routes are asserted to still answer a named pack (200), still answer an unknown pack (404 unknown city pack), and still refuse a tenant-private pack to an anonymous caller (401). The lane refuses an ABSENCE; it does not refuse the route.
runner.clientHarness: Assertions over web/app.js and web/index.html for the resolution order, the absence of any literal or default IN CODE (comments excluded, because the file explains why the default was deleted and a substring test cannot tell a symbol from a sentence about it), the loaders being inside the guard, the else branch calling showNoCityState(), the panel shipping hidden and not being a .lens, and a mutation test per property so the clean arm is not an unrun check.

proofOnTheDeployedSurface.method: The same probe script run twice against the same URL, unauthenticated - no bearer, no tenant key, no service key - which is the only way to turn 'the fix works' into 'the defect was here on the wire and now it is not'. The keyless refusal needs no credential, and a tenant-private pack's honest anonymous answer IS its access refusal.

preFixLeg.result: 5 of 7 probeable routes answered a request that named no city with 200 AND the demo pack's identity on the wire. The other two: shell state answered 200 without carrying the token, and finance sources - G-159's route, the control - answered 400 city_key_required.

postFixLeg.deployment: 84b9053f-2325-4a25-b2fd-6998a2e02591 at da3d611, read back immediately before
postFixLeg.result: 7 of 7 probeable routes refuse keyless, empty AND whitespace cityKey with 400 city_key_required, and 0 of 7 serve a resolved demo pack.
postFixLeg.fourCellsPerRoute: keyless 400 / bastrop_tx anonymously 401 / no-such-city 404 / template-city 200, on all seven. The unnamed-cell refusal is the change; the other three cells are unchanged from the pre-fix leg, which is what shows the lane refused an absence rather than breaking the route.
postFixLeg.theMunicodePostsCell: Its six cells are 401 in BOTH legs, because on a deployment that sets DASHBOARDS_API_KEY its caller-authorisation gate answers before its city refusal for an anonymous caller. Its 400 cell is therefore UNMEASURED on the deployed surface and is proven in src/city-refusal.test.mjs, which runs with the caller gate open. Stated rather than worked around, and deliberately NOT fixed by reordering the route's own authorisation gate to make this probe pass.
postFixLeg.clientReading: The probe's app.js block asks whether the shipped file still carries the default as CODE. It first answered TRUE post-fix, because the test was a substring over the whole file and web/app.js explains IN COMMENTS why the default was deleted. A field named for an import that answers a question about comment text is an instrument measuring itself, so the field is now computed over comment-stripped source (the same normalization src/city-resolution.test.mjs uses) and the raw substring is reported beside it as rawSubstringMentionsDefaultCityKey. Post-fix: importsDefaultCityKey false, resolvesCallerTenant true, showsNoCityState true, raw substring true.

theBareVisit.whyABrowserMeasurementAtAll: The route probe cannot distinguish 'the client was told no city' from 'the client guessed one'; only a rendered visit can. And the pre-fix leg could not be recovered after the deploy, because the deployment that served it is replaced.
theBareVisit.pre_fix_53ade8a: document.title 'Overview · Template city · SmartCity Dashboards'; all 17 city-name hooks read 'Template city'; no no-city panel; lens-city-manager visible. One city's name was in the browser tab and in every name hook, with nothing marking it as a default or a choice the visitor had not made.
theBareVisit.post_fix_da3d611: document.title 'Overview · SmartCity Dashboards' (no city name); all 17 hooks read the neutral 'This city'; all 15 .lens hidden; #no-city-state present, hidden=false, display=block, visible=true; 'Template city' and the literal 'template-city' appear NOWHERE in the document.
theBareVisit.deviationStatedNotWorkedAround: The post-fix leg has NO screenshot. browser_take_screenshot timed out twice while the machine was carrying 149 chrome processes, and it was not retried a third time: the measurement that matters is the DOM reading, which is captured verbatim in the artifact. Recorded rather than papered over, with the browser session (viewId 190544) named so the leg is reproducible.

theClientTransitionStateStated: Before the client's resolution settles - app.js awaits GET /api/city-packs before deciding - the static markup has lens-city-manager visible with its neutral 'This city' placeholders, which is G-89's designed scripting-off state. A bare visit therefore paints one generic lens briefly and then swaps to the no-city panel. This is stated because a reader of the accessibility snapshot taken immediately after navigation sees the lens content; the authoritative reading is the settled DOM, which is what the post-fix artifact records. Nothing in the transitional state names a city.
leaveBehind: THE DEMO'S PUBLIC URL. Under the operator's rule 3 ruling the demo becomes an explicit choice, so any surface that links to the demo must carry ?cityKey=template-city. Enumerated here so it is not discovered as a broken link: the a11y gate's targets all carry it now, and the gate is the instrument most likely to be pointed at the app by a later lane.

THE SECOND LEG IS THE ONE TO WATCH. The client's caller-tenant resolution reads GET /api/city-packs and takes caller.tenant. It is exercised for the anonymous case (null -> no-city state) in the test runner and on the deployed surface, but the SIGNED-IN case is not measurable without a staff session on d12-main-uat, so it is the one path this lane's live proof does not cover. A staff sign-in that resolves no tenant now sees the no-city panel rather than the demo pack, which is the intended behaviour and is also a visible change for staff who never named a city.

TWO SCRIPT-ARGUMENT DEFAULTS ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT, with their reasons, in CP1's enumeration: scripts/export-dev-services-lens.mjs:59 and scripts/export-finance-lens.mjs:33. They are operator-run tools with explicit arguments, not request-scoped defaults. A future lane that decides otherwise should find the reasoning rather than a bare line.
THE PRE-EXISTING src/server.test.mjs ECONNRESET FLAKE named in G-159's close did not reproduce here. It is still an unexplained flake in the suite and still wants an owner.

G-159's CP2 recorded that web/index.html carried 16 template-city literals and that src/city-identity.test.mjs's own comment asserts they exist. CP1 re-measured this: web/index.html carries ZERO at current main, because G-80 landed. The test still passes (it asserts absence) but its comment now describes a tree that no longer exists. Not this lane's file to edit, and worth a one-line correction by whoever owns it.
falsifier: Pre-registered in CP1 and honoured: if the demo's public demo depended on a bare visit landing on template-city, the operator would be asked rather than the lane choosing. It DID depend on it, the question was filed in CP1, and the operator selected strict rule 3 - so the lane deleted the dependency and the demo became an explicit choice rather than the lane quietly keeping a default to protect it. THE SECOND FALSIFIER, stated in the merge body before the deploy: if the client's second resolution leg had turned out to be something a browser cannot do, the strict no-city branch would have been unreachable for signed-in staff and this would have shipped as a regression for every staff user rather than a fix. It was measured instead of assumed, and the route returns the caller's own resolved tenant with null as a real state.
contradicted: The dispatch enumerates the work as seven server routes plus the client, and the count is right, but the shape it implies is not: the a11y gate was a SIXTH surface that had to change in the same commit, and it is not mentioned in the dispatch. It had been built on the client's default - its targets deliberately carried no cityKey - so deleting the default without touching it would have turned the first red gate on this lane into a red on every title, for a reason that had nothing to do with accessibility. Found by reading the instrument rather than by running it. SECOND: the probe script this lane itself wrote reported the post-fix app.js as still importing the default, because its substring test could not tell an import from a comment about one. That is the same defect class G-154 spent a whole lane on in this repo, found here in a file written by this lane, and fixed by changing the instrument rather than by softening the comment.
